test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 Oct 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All Umbrellas are Raincoats.

All Raincoats are Frogs.

Some Raincoats are Water.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Frogs are Water.

(II) All Umbrellas are Frogs.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b920f014ee271f447927d091cbf979ccec8cc78aecb23ff5c554677d4fe738e.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some Frogs are Water → Follow (As all Raincoats are Frogs and some Raincoats are Water. As whole raincoats comes in frogs and has some part common with water, therefore it is true.)

(II) All Umbrellas are Frogs → Follow (As all Umbrellas are Raincoats and all Raincoats are Frogs. As whole umbrellas comes in raincoats which whole comes in frogs, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
